President Donald Trump unleashed another fierce attack on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Wednesday, calling him “stupid” and accusing him of costing the country “a fortune.” Speaking just hours before the Federal Open Market Committee’s highly anticipated decision on interest rates, Trump said Powell “just refuses to lower the Fed rate” and questioned his intelligence and political motives.
Turning to the broader economic picture, the Federal Reserve currently holds the overnight borrowing rate between 4.25% and 4.50%, with market expectations indicating no cut at this meeting.
The Fed has expressed caution about adjusting rates amid ongoing uncertainty, particularly over the long-term effects of Trump’s tariffs.
Inflation indicators have remained relatively stable since the tariffs were implemented in April, dampening calls for immediate rate changes.

Trump criticized the higher interest rates, claiming they are costing the US “hundreds of billions” in financing costs that could be saved if the Fed eased monetary policy. “If he’s worried about inflation, that’s OK.
I don’t think there’s going to be any.
So far there hasn’t,” he said.
Despite recent meetings between Trump and Powell at the White House, little is known about their discussions.
Powell and the Fed have vowed to remain independent and resist political pressure, even as it intensifies from Trump and other administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance.

Trump even mused about taking over the Fed chairmanship himself, declaring, “I’d do a much better job than these people.” With Powell’s term set to expire in May 2026, Trump has indicated he plans to name a successor soon.
